$comment: scripts/check-neutral-names.mjs reads this. See scripts/lib/neutral-names.mjs for what each section means. Contracts and examples are exact names; base_word gives a per-file ceiling for the bare word and must equal today's count. record_words is the second ratchet (scripts/lib/record-words.mjs): which files are read for the record words written as prose, the names that are not prose, and a per-file ceiling for what remains.

exempt_paths.$comment: Whole paths the check does not read, each for a reason that does not expire with a rename.
exempt_paths.drizzle/meta/: migration history: the journal's schema snapshots are immutable records of what each migration produced; rewriting one would make drift lie
exempt_paths.scripts/fixtures/: pinned before-images: the pre-rename package surface, the default profile's model-facing surface and an old schema, kept verbatim so tests can prove the migrations and translations against them
exempt_paths.scripts/fde/lib/: two one-line re-exports kept at the operator tooling's old lib paths (customer.mjs, which the software factory's workspace seeding imports, and the old helpers module), so an import written against the old path still resolves; the code is in scripts/operator/lib/
exempt_paths.scripts/lib/neutral-names.mjs: the check, which has to describe what it matches
exempt_paths.scripts/test-neutral-names.mjs: the check's test, which constructs an offender of every kind
exempt_paths.package-lock.json: the root package's name (`fde-agent`, an infrastructure name) as npm records it

contracts.$comment: Exact names that something outside this repository already holds. Each moves by an additive migration with the old name kept working; the plan says which PR. A name listed here that no longer occurs anywhere fails the check.

base_word.$comment: Per file, the exact count of the bare word today, grouped by why it may stay. More fails; fewer fails with the number to lower it to.

legacy.why: The member's legacy word itself, spelled once: agent/lib/legacy-member.ts holds it (singular, plural, owner phrase) for the machinery that still meets it in contract identifiers, stored values and older text (the vocabulary translates it under a relabelling profile; the UI shows a stored value in the profile's member word), and scripts/lib/agent-cli.mjs holds BASE_PRODUCT_WORD, the lower-case spelling every gate and test that refuses the word builds its pattern from. Base text never spells it: it writes role placeholders ({member}, {owner}) the profile fills (PR 6).

stored.why: Stored enum values (a ticket's `ownerTeam: "<legacy word>"`, a value-evidence status `"<legacy word> Verified"`) and the sample and fixture records that carry them. Rows are never rewritten here: changing a stored value is a data migration. A person reads them in the profile's member word (storedValueLabel in lib/ui-words.ts); the model writes them back as stored, like a column name, and check:agent-vocabulary allows exactly these values in a tool schema.

record_words.$comment: The record words (customer, deployment, implementation, rollout; any case, singular or plural) written as PROSE in text base code hands to a reader: string literals, template text and JSX text of source files, Markdown, the string values of JSON. Base text writes a placeholder the profile fills instead ({account}, {deployment}, {implementation}, {rollout}; agent/lib/agent-vocabulary.ts) or takes the word from lib/ui-words.ts. Identifiers, paths, code spans, quoted values and one-token strings are never counted. `node scripts/check-neutral-names.mjs --records --lines` lists what is left.

scan.$comment: Globs of the files read. Everything a model or a person is handed by base code; not docs, tests, comments or migrations.
scan.agent/**: the agent: prompts, tool and parameter descriptions, messages, skills and sandbox files
scan.app/**: the web app and its API messages
scan.lib/**: server and client libraries whose strings reach a page, an API answer or a seeded file
scan.skills/**: the base skill a coding assistant installs
scan.setup/skills/**: the base skill as the generic package ships it (filled from the default profile)
scan.scripts/operator/**: the library workflows and the operator tooling
scan.scripts/seed*: the seeders: what a new data room and a demo database are filled with
scan.profiles/00-default.json: the default profile: the words every placeholder is filled with
scan.dm.md: the data-room description served to coding assistants

skip.$comment: Globs left out of the scan, each for a reason.
skip.**/*.generated.*: derived from a scanned source (prompts, the profile, the workflow library, the subagent registry)
skip.agent/lib/agent-vocabulary.ts: the vocabulary machinery: it names the legacy words to translate them (LEGACY_RECORDS) and its comments' examples are not text anyone is handed
skip.**/__fixtures__/**: fixture records: stored data, not base text

names.$comment: Whole names that are not prose where they stand: a specialist's directory name (hyphenated anywhere; a single word only when written **bold** or as code), and stored enum values and sheet names of more than one word. Each is a contract.
names.customer-context: specialist directory name: the model delegates to it by this name
names.deployment: specialist directory name (allowed as **deployment** in a roster line)
names.customer-vpc: stored enum value (deployment region / hosting model)
names.Customer Stakeholders: workbook sheet name (People/Master.xlsx), a contract of the data model
names.new-customer: npm script and operator tool name (operator:new-customer), a contract (scripts/test-operator-tooling.mjs)

ceilings.$comment: Per file, the exact count of record words written as prose today, grouped by why they remain. More fails; fewer fails with the number to lower it to; a ceiling on a file that carries none fails. The agent side (prompts, tool and parameter descriptions, messages, the library workflows, the base skill, the default profile, the operator tooling) carries none: PR 7a.

stored.why: A stored enum value that is the record word itself (`blockerOwner: "Customer"`, a ticket's waiting party). Rows are never rewritten here: changing a stored value is a data migration. A relabelling profile's reader gets the profile's label for it (domains.<area>.fields.<key>.options).

ui.why: The web app, its API messages and the libraries behind them (app/, components/, lib/): PR 7b of mold_v1-103 owns these and lowers each ceiling as it takes the word from lib/ui-words.ts (W.account, W.deployments, …) or fills a placeholder. Counted at the commit PR 7a branched from.

seeders.why: The seeders (scripts/seed*): the sample data room and demo database they write. PR 7b of mold_v1-103 owns these; sample CONTENT (a fictional account's notes) is data and may stay under its ceiling, the seeders' own labels and messages move to the profile's words.

rig.why: A performance rig's synthetic chat content (a made-up table and the question asked about it): never shown to a deployment's reader and not base text, but under scripts/operator/ and so read by the scan.
